courses.title: Backup & restore: tar, rsync and strategy
courses.summary: Design and run real backups: 3-2-1, RPO/RTO, tar archives and compression, rsync incremental mirrors and hard-link snapshots, database dumps, verification and restore drills. Independent practice material; not affiliated with or endorsed by the exam provider. Check the official exam guide for the current skills outline.
outcomes: Learners can define RPO/RTO and a 3-2-1 strategy
Learners can create, list and extract tar archives
Learners can mirror and snapshot with rsync
Learners can test restores and document them

lessons.title: Backup strategy: 3-2-1, RPO and RTO

scenes.text: A small firm's NAS — and its attached USB backup — were encrypted together.
Strategy matters more than tools.

steps.title: Concepts
steps.body:
- **3-2-1**: 3 copies, 2 different media, 1 off-site (many add: 1 immutable/offline, 0 errors after verification)
- **RPO** (Recovery Point Objective): max acceptable data loss in time → backup frequency
- **RTO** (Recovery Time Objective): max acceptable downtime → restore speed
- Full vs incremental vs differential

steps.title: Solved example
steps.body: Shop DB: RPO 1 h, RTO 4 h → hourly binlog/incremental + nightly full; tested restore must finish < 4 h.

steps.title: Untested backups
steps.body: A backup is only real when a restore has been tested.

activity.prompt: Match term to definition
pairs: Changes since the last backup of any kind
Changes since the last full backup

options: You may lose at most 15 minutes of data
quiz.why: Correct answer: You may lose at most 15 minutes of data.

quiz.q: Restoring needs full + every incremental since — which type?
Why was the USB backup lost?
options: It was online/attached — same blast radius
quiz.why: Correct answer: It was online/attached — same blast radius.

lessons.title: Lab: tar archives

scenes.text: Before a major upgrade, Nisha archives /etc and the app directory.
tar with compression, listing and selective extraction.

steps.title: tar
steps.body:
- Create: `tar czf etc-2026-11-26.tar.gz /etc` (z gzip, j bzip2, J xz, `--zstd`)
- List: `tar tzf file`
- Extract: `tar xzf file -C /restore`
- One file: `tar xzf file etc/ssh/sshd_config -C /tmp`
- Preserve: `-p` perms (default for root), `--acls --xattrs --selinux`

steps.title: Leading /
steps.body: tar strips the leading / ('Removing leading `/' from member names') so extraction goes relative to -C — a safety feature.

steps.title: Exclude
steps.body: `--exclude='*.log' --exclude=/srv/app/tmp`

activity.prompt: Archive /etc with gzip and SELinux/ACL attributes, list it, and restore only etc/ssh/sshd_config into /tmp/restore.

responses.out: tar: Removing leading `/' from member names

options: So extraction doesn't overwrite absolute system paths unexpectedly
quiz.why: Correct answer: So extraction doesn't overwrite absolute system paths unexpectedly.

lessons.title: Lab: rsync mirrors and hard-link snapshots

scenes.text: Nisha needs nightly copies of /srv/data (800 GB) — copying everything each night is impossible.
rsync sends only changes; --link-dest makes daily snapshots cheap.

steps.title: rsync
steps.body:
- `rsync -aHAX --delete /srv/data/ backup01:/backups/data/` (a archive, H hard links, A ACLs, X xattrs)
- Trailing slash on source = copy **contents**
- `-n` dry-run, `--info=progress2`, `--bwlimit=50M`
- Snapshots: `rsync -a --link-dest=../2026-11-25 /srv/data/ /backups/2026-11-26/` — unchanged files are hard links (no extra space)

steps.title: Slash rule
steps.body: `rsync -a /srv/data backup:/b/` → /b/data/…; `rsync -a /srv/data/ backup:/b/` → /b/… directly.

steps.title: --delete danger
steps.body: With a wrong path, --delete wipes the destination. Always dry-run (-n) first.

lessons.title: Lab: Database dumps

scenes.text: Copying /var/lib/mysql of a running DB gives a corrupt backup.
Use the DB's own tools.

steps.title: Logical dumps
steps.body:
- `mariadb-dump --single-transaction --routines --triggers --all-databases | gzip > all-$(date +%F).sql.gz` (InnoDB consistent without locking)
- `mysqldump` is the compatible name
- PostgreSQL: `pg_dump -Fc dbname > db.dump`, restore `pg_restore`
- Physical hot backups: `mariadb-backup` / `pg_basebackup`

steps.title: Restore test
steps.body: `gunzip < shop.sql.gz | mariadb shop_restore_test` then compare row counts.

steps.title: Credentials
steps.body: Don't put passwords on the command line (visible in ps). Use `~/.my.cnf` with mode 600.

lessons.title: Lab: Capstone · Restore drill

scenes.text: The auditor asks: 'Show me a restore of last night's file server backup.'

steps.title: Drill
steps.body:
1. Pick a random backup and file set
2. Restore to an isolated location
3. Verify integrity (checksums, app opens, row counts)
4. Time it vs RTO
5. Record evidence, issues and improvements

steps.title: Checksums
steps.body: `sha256sum -c manifest.sha256` → all OK. Manifests created at backup time make verification objective.

steps.title: Cadence
steps.body: Quarterly restore tests for critical systems are a common policy.
